correctness.rationale: Explicit degree-two quotient maps yield complementary holomorphic differential subspaces, hence an isogeny in odd characteristic. The birational inversion gives the -1 quadratic twist, and complete F_11 and F_121 point enumeration produces genus-two coefficients. The functional equation determines all remaining coefficients; an independent direct count of the genus-four curve agrees. The mod-3 quartic factor test proves both abelian surfaces are simple over F_11; distinct Frobenius factors prove nonisogeny and the twist becomes isomorphic over F_121. All steps and exact code are included.

value.rationale: The genus-four Accola–Maclachlan curve is a canonical high-symmetry curve whose two geometric simple factors were a specific subject of the 2024 paper. At the smallest good prime splitting in Q(zeta_5), its two factors have different rational Frobenius spectra and are not even isogenous, despite becoming isomorphic over the quadratic extension. This is an arithmetic descent obstruction for a motivated distinguished Jacobian, with complete and independently reproducible local invariants; it is not merely a generic quotient identity or arbitrary parameter slice.
